extracted.intended_audience: government lawyers, military administrators, and claimants handling volunteer service/muster legal issues
extracted.subtask_description: Legal rules and standards governing the status, muster-in, retention, transfer, and muster-out of volunteer and militia forces of the United States (historical/opinion-based guidance drawn from War Department/Attorney General opinions and General Orders).

rubrics_metrics.name: State militia status on transfer to U.S. service
rubrics_metrics.description: When State militia organizations are transferred to the service of the United States (under a Presidential call), they retain their character as State militia and at the same time, while in active United States service, are part of the Army of the United States (the Volunteer Army).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies even where men were conscripted into State militia against their will; once called into U.S. service their status is as militia called into U.S. service and generally considered part of the Volunteer Army.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and statutory dependency of 'volunteers'
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'volunteers' is usually applied to soldiers of a temporary United States Army raised, organized, supported, and maintained for a limited period by the United States independently of any State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The President cannot raise and maintain such a volunteer army at any time without express authority of Congress; statutes authorizing raising/employing volunteers are decisive for their legal status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of volunteer versus militia status depends on statutory authority
rubrics_metrics.description: If volunteers actually performed service at a time when an act of Congress authorized them to be raised, maintained, and employed, their status is determined to be that of Volunteers; absent such statutory authorization, their claim to volunteer status must fail even if paid or recognized administratively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive recognition or payment alone cannot substitute for statutory authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteer force during Civil War = part of U.S. Army (not militia)
rubrics_metrics.description: During the Civil War the Volunteer force was not part of the militia but of the Army of the United States; assimilated in some respects but legally distinct from militia and similar in status to Regular officers once mustered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Volunteer officers, once mustered into U.S. service and while remaining in it, did not differ substantially from Regular officers in status or rights (aside from typically briefer tenure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Officers of the Volunteer Army are officers of the United States
rubrics_metrics.description: All officers of the Volunteer Army are officers of the United States once properly mustered into U.S. service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper muster is a prerequisite to vesting the United States office/status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruits mustered directly into United States service
rubrics_metrics.description: Under laws relating to raising U.S. Volunteers, recruits are mustered/enlisted directly into the service of the United States and become soldiers on completion of enlistment procedures (e.g., taking the oath of allegiance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule was applied during the Spanish War and similar authorizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance into U.S. service requires formal muster in by authorized officer
rubrics_metrics.description: No regiment, company, or other volunteer organization can be regarded as having been 'accepted' into the military service of the United States until it has been formally mustered into such service by a commissioned officer of the Army duly authorized by the Secretary of War.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to such muster, persons who enroll or indicate intent remain under exclusive jurisdiction and control of their State governors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Muster-in transfers jurisdiction from State to United States
rubrics_metrics.description: By undergoing 'muster in' organizations of Volunteers are 'accepted' into U.S. military service and pass out of State control into the exclusive control and jurisdiction of the United States as part of its volunteer forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While in recruitment/organization the State's jurisdiction is plenary until formal muster in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enrollment is only a proposal; acceptance requires two acts of volition
rubrics_metrics.description: A volunteer soldier's entry into service depends on two acts of volition: (1) the offer/enrollment to enter service and (2) the acceptance of that offer by a duly authorized U.S. representative (manifested by muster in).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enrollment alone does not create U.S. soldier status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive muster-in doctrine
rubrics_metrics.description: A muster in is not necessarily formal; placing a man on duty, availing of his services, treating him as in military service, paying him as a soldier, or listing him on rolls may constitute a constructive muster in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many opinions find such conduct equivalent to formal muster when the Government has accepted and used the person's services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Person paid and performing duties may be treated as duly enlisted absent signed articles
rubrics_metrics.description: A man who has been duly mustered into service and has received pay and performed duties of a soldier should be treated as duly enlisted even if he did not sign enlistment articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical recognition by payment and service can substitute for formal enlistment signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation does not require remuster
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a regiment is consolidated with another under the name of the latter, no remuster or change in status of enlisted men is necessary; men of each organization become members of the new regiment by virtue of the conditions of their original enlistment and muster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No consent by enlisted men is required for the change in organization status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Muster-in not necessary for drafted men or substitutes when put on duty
rubrics_metrics.description: A muster in is not necessary for a drafted man or substitute; examining him, holding him to service, and actually putting him on duty takes the place of the muster-in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical induction into service suffices for drafted individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official muster records are conclusive absent fraud
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of a formal muster in is an official record made pursuant to law; in the absence of fraud it is conclusive evidence of the facts recorded and other evidence is inadmissible to show a different state of facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitting parol evidence to set aside such records would create great uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Muster-in as final act closing contract and irrevocability
rubrics_metrics.description: A muster in is the final act which closes a contract between a person and the Government and fixes relations between them; a legal muster in is irrevocable except where tainted with fraud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Muster in creates binding legal obligations between soldier and Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: State appointments not vesting U.S. office without muster
rubrics_metrics.description: A man commissioned under a State appointment but not formally mustered into U.S. service does not, in the absence of special Congressional provision, hold a U.S. military office or status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mustering officer refusal to muster an appointee prevents vesting of the U.S. office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Some civilian 'volunteer' organizations not authorized as U.S. volunteers
rubrics_metrics.description: Groups like the Quartermaster's Volunteers (clerks/civilian employees) were not authorized by statute to be formed into a volunteer organization, were not mustered into military service, and their officers did not hold military office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory authorization is required to form/pay/muster such organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfers and enlistments into Regular Army allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Volunteer soldiers may be transferred to the Regular Army and serve unexpired terms; statutes allow transfers (historical examples cited).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific statutes (e.g., March 1, 1887) govern certain transfers (e.g., to the Hospital Corps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Muster-out orders by War Department have force of law
rubrics_metrics.description: An order issued by the War Department directing muster out of volunteer troops must be regarded as promulgated by authority and is a regulation with reference to Army administration which the President has constitutional authority to make; as such it has the force of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General Orders effect administrative law governing muster out.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Orders: muster out treats whole organization as mustered out except certain absentees
rubrics_metrics.description: General Orders (e.g., No. 108, 124, 13) provided that when an organization is mustered out the whole organization is considered mustered out except certain classes of absentees; under later regulations retention in service after muster out must be by special War Department authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retention requires competent/special authority; otherwise absentees are discharged with the organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order purporting to dismiss an officer already mustered out is void
rubrics_metrics.description: An order purported to dismiss an officer who has been mustered out of the service is absolutely void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Muster out is final and terminates military jurisdiction over the individual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Muster-out is formal discharge converting soldier to civilian
rubrics_metrics.description: The muster out is a formal discharge from the Army, making a soldier a civilian and terminating all military authority and jurisdiction over him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As muster in converts civilian to soldier, muster out converts soldier to civilian; effects include transportation/subsistence as a former soldier may be provided as a matter of fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discharge certificate not necessary to effect muster out
rubrics_metrics.description: A discharge certificate is not necessary to effect a muster out, since the muster out itself is the formal discharge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However discharge papers may be issued and have evidentiary weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention in service after muster out: general rule and definition of competent authority
rubrics_metrics.description: As a general rule, an officer or enlisted man of Volunteers who was not actually mustered out with his command must be considered retained in U.S. service if he was retained by competent authority; 'competent authority' is the order of any superior whom the person was duty-bound to respect and obey and who could exercise control over the subordinate while in service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retention by competent authority means the individual remains in military service until properly discharged; exceptions exist for deserters, absentees, or those retained solely for their own comfort (sick/wounded) without control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absentees and deserters at muster out are generally discharged unless retained
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers and enlisted men retained for service or convenience of Government (or by refusal/neglect of superiors) are not mustered out with their organization; but deserters at large or absentees (with or without leave) at the date of muster out are not retained and thus are not mustered out with their organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retention must be contemporaneous by competent authority; mere absence or personal fault does not count as retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention after muster out valid for court-martial
rubrics_metrics.description: It is proper to retain in service officers or enlisted men of Volunteer forces after muster out of their regiments for the purpose of bringing them to trial by court-martial for offenses charged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retention for disciplinary/legal purposes is within competent authority powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: True date of muster out is the actual date of muster out
rubrics_metrics.description: The true date of muster out is the date when the organization or individual was actually mustered out; when official records clearly show an actual date that date should be accepted regardless of pre-fixed dates, payment dates, or discharge certificate dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an individual is retained after his command's muster out, discharge takes effect on the date he receives notice of discharge (or date of the discharge order) provided he obeyed orders without delay; otherwise on the organization's muster-out date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special prisoner-of-war rule for muster-out timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Under General Orders, soldiers who were prisoners of war when their company was mustered out were to be considered in service until arrival in a loyal State, with allowance for travel time; their muster-out date is the date designated for them to report after release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: soldier released from captivity then furloughed and ordered to report at a post — he is in service until that designated report date and mustered out on that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directory statutory provisions do not automatically invalidate extended service
rubrics_metrics.description: Where statutes (e.g., requiring mustering out within X days) are directory only, failure of proper officer to muster out at the precise statutory date does not invalidate service continued beyond that time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service continued due to administrative failure remains valid absent other legal defect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial congressional payment as recognition of lack of prior status
rubrics_metrics.description: Remedial legislation by Congress to pay volunteers the same as Regular Army officers and soldiers has been interpreted as specific recognition that those persons were not officers and soldiers during the earlier period (otherwise remedial legislation would not have been needed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Congressional remedies can serve as retrospective recognition or correction of legal status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date-of-muster-out rules for absent men
rubrics_metrics.description: General Orders fix the policy that volunteers absent at the date of muster out of their organizations shall be held to have been mustered out on that date unless retained by competent authority; however where an absent soldier is not actually mustered out on that date (e.g., absent in hospital) he may be mustered out later when notified or when he reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different categories (absent with leave, absent without leave, prisoners, hospitalized) have specific applications under General Orders and precedent.
